title: Renting vs buying in Niagara: how to decide what's right for you
excerpt: Should you keep renting or buy a home in St. Catharines or Niagara? The key questions to ask before you decide.
content:
Renting and buying both have real advantages. The right choice depends less on the market headlines and more on your finances, your plans and your lifestyle.

The case for buying

  • Building equity: each mortgage payment pays down your loan, instead of your landlord's
  • Stability: no surprise move-outs, and you control renovations and decor
  • Long-term value: real estate has historically appreciated over the long run, though nothing is guaranteed

The case for renting

  • Flexibility: easier to move for work or a change of plans
  • Lower upfront cost: no down payment or closing costs
  • Predictable expenses: major repairs are the landlord's responsibility

Questions to ask yourself

  1. How long do you plan to stay in the area? Buying generally makes more sense the longer you stay.
  2. Do you have a down payment plus an emergency fund?
  3. How stable is your income?
  4. How does a mortgage payment, plus taxes, insurance and maintenance, compare to your rent?

Run the numbers

Use the mortgage calculator to compare estimated payments with your current rent, then talk to a lender about pre-approval to see what's realistic.
